data.name: Sherlock Holmes: The Silver Earring
data.detailed_description:
Destaque


Acerca do jogo

Numa receção organizada em honra da sua filha, Melvyn Bromsby, um rico empresário, está prestes a fazer uma importante declaração quanto ao futuro dos negócios quando, de repente, um tiro é disparado. Sir Bromsby cai, vítima de um ferimento fatal no coração...
Um assassinato inexplicável, dezenas de testemunhas e numerosos lugares para visitar em Londres da era Vitoriana. Tu desempenhas o papel de Sherlock Holmes, e usas todas as tuas habilidades para resolver este misterioso caso.
  • Assume o papel de Sherlock Holmes e do Doutor Watson e conhece todos os heróis dos livros: Inspetor Lestrade, Wiggins, Mycroft e muitos outros!
  • Investiga 5 assassinatos! Mais de 40 testemunhas para interrogar, 200 pistas para descobrir e mais de 25 horas de jogabilidade para resolver o mistério.
  • Explora Londres da era Vitoriana, magnificamente e fielmente reproduzida em 3D.
  • Entre cada nível Sherlock Holmes testa os teus conhecimentos, validando o teu progresso no caso.
  • A aventura está repleta de vívidas cenas de vídeo, realçando o aspecto dramático da história.

data.short_description: Melvyn Bromsby, a rich tycoon, is about to make a statement, when suddenly a shot rings out. Sir Bromsby collapses - a mortal wound to the heart... A baffling murder, dozens of witnesses and no suspects! You, Sherlock Holmes, must use all your skills to shed light on this mysterious case.

reviews.review:
Archaic, trial-and-error progression and broken gameplay mechanics that turn a classic murder mystery into a frustrating technical headache.

If you are thinking of picking up Sherlock Holmes: The Silver Earring, it is a mechanically broken point-and-click entry that manages to ruin its authentic Victorian atmosphere with abysmal design choices. While the foundational premise of solving a high-profile mansion murder sounds like a classic Doyle adventure, the execution relies on archaic systems, terrible controls, and sudden gameplay shifts that feel outright malicious.

Here is what you need to know before diving in:

• Tank Controls in Water: Navigating the pre-rendered 3D environments is an absolute nightmare. The character pathfinding and collision detection are completely broken; clicking on a destination often results in Sherlock doing awkward, robotic spins or outright ignoring your commands. Trying to maneuver him into specific rooms or narrow corridors feels like trying to steer a shopping cart with broken wheels.

• Absurdly Unfair "Deadly" Puzzles: The game randomly abandons its traditional investigation style to throw you into atrocious, unprompted timed sequences. At one point, you are forced to run through a dark woodland maze on a strict time limit to fetch a bucket of water to put out a fire, with no clear indication of where the bucket even was. Combined with the sluggish character movement, these instances lead to instant, repetitive failure screens.

• Broken Logic Quizzes: At the end of each in-game day, you are locked into a mandatory, pedantic quiz before you can progress. You must answer a series of questions and tie them exactly to matching clues and journal entries. Because of terrible localizations and translation errors, the logic falls completely flat; the game will reject your perfectly accurate evidence simply because it wants a different, ambiguous journal entry that might not even show up properly in your menu.

• Trial-and-Error Stealth: One of the most infamously awful segments requires you to sneak past a guard dog at night. The dog essentially possesses x-ray vision, triggering an instant game-over from massive distances regardless of whether you are standing behind solid walls or environment assets. It forces you into a brutal cycle of quick-saving and reloading just to guess the exact, arbitrary path the developers expected you to walk.

Final Verdict: A structurally flawed puzzle hunt that replaces brilliant investigation with artificial friction. If you don't want to wrestle with clunky point-and-click navigation, unpolished logic tests, and immersion-breaking instant deaths, save yourself the headache and skip this entry entirely.
